summary: Bronwyn Finnigan is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the universities of Melbourne, Sydney, and Auckland under Rosalind Hursthouse and John Bishop. She held posts at Auckland (~2009–2013), Marquette (2012–2014), and the Australian National University (2014).

Brook Ziporyn specializes in sinology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Chicago, under Yiyun Xing, and completed his PhD under Donald J. Munro at Michigan. He held posts at Northwestern (~1999–2012), NUS (~2012–2013), and the University of Chicago (~2013, ~2016).
Brooke Schedneck works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Arizona State University under the supervision of Juliane Schober.

Bruce B. Lawrence is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. Educated at Fay School, Princeton University (~1958–1962), and the Episcopal Divinity School (~1966–1969), he served as a professor at Duke University from ~1971 to ~2008.

Bruce Charles Williams is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied under Edward H. Schafer, Michael C. Rogers, Michel Strickmann, Barend A. van Nooten, Padmanabh S. Jaini, and Akira Fujieda.
Bruce Chilton works in religious studies. He studied at St John's College (~1971–1977) and held positions at Yale University (~1985–1987) and Bard College (~1987).

Bruce John Stewart specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Sakya College in 1978 and earned his PhD at Columbia University under Alex Wayman (attested 1983), also studying under Joel Brereton and Christopher S. George.

Bruce Kapferer is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at the University of Sydney and the University of Manchester under Max Gluckman. His career includes posts at Adelaide, Gothenburg, UCL, James Cook University, and Bergen.

Bruce Lincoln specializes in religious studies, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Haverford and the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade, later holding posts at Minnesota (1976–1994) and Chicago (~1993).
Bruce M. Sullivan was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under J. A. B. van Buitenen (~1974–1979) and held an academic post at Northern Arizona University from ~1990 to 2021.

Bruce Matthews works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. After graduate studies at McMaster University (~1970–1974), he held positions at the University of Ceylon and as C. B. Lumsden Professor of Comparative Religion at Acadia University (~1976–2006).
Bruce McCoy Owens works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held appointments at Columbia University (attested 1988) and Wheaton College (attested 2019).

Bruce Schneier works in computational and other fields. Educated at Hunter College High School, Rochester, and American University, he held posts at BT (~2006–2013), Harvard (~2014), IBM (2016–2019), Inrupt (~2019), and Toronto (attested 2026).

Bruno Dagens was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology who studied under Colette Caillat. He held posts at the EFEO (1969), KU Leuven (1972–1977), the French Institute of Pondicherry (1977), and Sorbonne Nouvelle University (1986).
Bruno Galasek is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Bonn under the supervision of Konrad Klaus (attested 2016).

Bruno Liebich was an Indologist who studied at Munich, Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn, and Breslau. He served as professor at the University of Breslau (attested 1902, 1921–1928) and later held a post at Heidelberg University (~1928–1939).
Bruno Lindner was an Indologist who studied at the University of Leipzig and under Rudolf von Roth (~1874–1878). He served as Privatdozent at the University of Leipzig from 1878 to 1919.

Bruno Petzold was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Leipzig and Strasbourg, and under Hikoshiro Hoshino and Daito Shimaji. He taught at First Higher School (1917–1943), Chuo University, Rissho University, and Seikei Senior High School.
Bruno Schindler was a sinologist who studied under August Conrady (~1910–1919) and founded Asia Major in 1923. He later worked as a Verlagslektor at Lund Humphries (~1939–1964).

Bryan D. Lowe is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at Otani University, with Jacqueline I. Stone as graduate advisor, and under several other teachers. He held a post at Vanderbilt University (attested 2017).
